1.1Cron job silently expired

Runbook — reference mode. Follow the phases top to bottom; don't skip the verify step.

LIVE
RUNBOOK-07 · Operational procedure
A recurring cron job stopped firing and nobody was notified — here's how to confirm it, recover it, and prevent the next silent expiry.
Session-only cron jobs auto-expire after 7 days with no notification. This is the recovery path, not a permanent fix.
scope: single sessiondowntime: none (read-only diagnosis)
DANGER: skipping verifyCAUTION: destructive step in phase 3INFO: safe to re-run
Irreversible or high-blast-radius — read twice before runningReversible but changes state — confirm the target firstRead-only — safe to run repeatedly while diagnosing

Is the job actually gone, or just quiet?

Re-arm the job — this is the destructive step

Verify
Confirm it actually fires before you walk away
5-30 min wait
Phase 3 changes state — confirm the job name before running.
Re-arming with the wrong job name creates a second, orphaned job instead of fixing the original. There is no automatic dedup.
  • CronList()Phase 1 — lists every active job for this session; the missing job confirms expiry, not crash
  • Check session agePhase 2 — if the job's session has been alive 7+ days, this is the known auto-expiry, not a bug
  • CronCreate(same schedule, same prompt)Phase 3 — re-arms the job under a NEW session-scoped id; the old id is gone for good
  • CronList() again, then wait one cyclePhase 4 — confirm the new job appears AND actually fires once before considering this closed
Recovered
Job re-armed and confirmed firing

Recovery is complete only after phase 4's wait — a job that lists but never fires is still broken, and re-arming does not guarantee the underlying cause (session death, host restart) won't repeat it.

Prevent the next one.
Session-only cron cannot be made durable from inside a session. If this job matters across restarts, it needs to move to a durably-scheduled mechanism outside this runbook's scope — file that as a follow-up, don't try to patch it here.
